title: LexiLearn Coach: Add Feature Component Name to Model Metadata
description: The LexiLearn Coach platform is used by data scientists to train and serve NLP models. For better model lineage and traceability, the MLOps team requires that all newly trained models have metadata indicating which feature extraction component was used. This task involves updating the core model data structures, modifying the training pipeline to populate this new information, and ensuring the new metadata is correctly saved and loaded from the artifact store.

project_spec.name: LexiLearn Coach: Component-Based NLP Tutor Platform
project_spec.description:
LexiLearn Coach is a medium-complexity machine-learning NLP platform written in C that allows schools and educational-technology vendors to build, train, deploy, and continuously improve personalized language-learning tutors.  Learners interact with the system through text prompts (e.g., essay answers, vocabulary drills, comprehension questions).  The system scores, gives formative feedback, and adapts future content based on each student’s lexical, syntactic, and semantic skill profile.  

Built with a pure component-based architecture, every pedagogical or MLOps concern—tokenization, feature engineering, experiment tracking, visualization, hyper-parameter exploration, model registry, and automated retraining—lives in its own loadable C module with clearly defined Strategy interfaces.  The Pipeline Pattern chains these interchangeable Strategy components to create learning pathways such as “Essay-Scoring > Misconception-Mining > Recommendation.”  All artifacts (datasets, features, and trained models) are stored in a versioned Feature Store and Model Registry, enabling reliable rollbacks, A/B classroom experiments, and compliant audit trails for educators.

MLOps pipelines trigger unattended nightly retraining when new annotated essays or quizzes are pushed from the Learning Management System.  Dashboards rendered with an embedded GUI library allow teachers to visualize cohort progress and inspect model drift, while administrators can spin up lightweight HTTP model-serving endpoints on school servers or low-cost edge devices, guaranteeing data privacy.
dependencies: liblinear / libsvm-core                – fast classical models for baselines
ONNX Runtime (C interface)             – model interoperability & serving
SQLite3                                – lightweight feature store / metadata DB
cJSON                                  – config, experiment, and registry files
libcurl                                – REST hooks for experiment tracking & LMS integration
GNU Scientific Library (GSL)           – statistics for data visualization
Dear ImGui (C binding)                 – in-app teacher dashboards
libgit2                                – versioning of datasets, features, and models
